Summary of what I saved (this was a near-miss worth capturing — close numeric error, generalizable cause):

What was learned: 109660 vs gold 109625 (~0.03% high) on a multi-step chain ending in a USD->GBP conversion. That magnitude of error isn't a value misread — it's exchange-rate precision and/or premature rounding.

Recorded as a new reference file in the existing skill (memory was full, and this is procedural anyway):
- references/currency-and-geomean.md — the durable, generalizable guidance:
  - Carry full float precision through every step; round only the final integer.
  - USD->GBP means DIVIDE by USD-per-GBP (~2.7913 in 1964, IMF/Fed annual average); using a coarse 2.79 makes the result slightly high.
  - "slightly high + otherwise correct" => under-divided => rate rounded down => add decimal places.
  - geometric mean = (prod of ratios)**(1/N); never arithmetic-mean, never round individual ratios first.
  - Statutory-debt-limitation table row labels to read exactly, and a note that mid-century fiscal-year-ends are odd dates (Feb 29 1960, etc.), not June 30.
- Added a one-line pointer in SKILL.md so a future agent discovers it.

I edited SKILL.md in place via the patch tool because the file now exceeds the skill-manage full-write size cap — splitting detail into references/ is the intended pattern here.
